**Reminder**: Yihui has released a fig.note option for `knitr`. https://github.com/yihui/knitr/pull/2453. Install development version and try it when you build the PDF.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(glue)

proj_root <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::is_git_root)
source(file.path(proj_root, "helpers", "bootstrap_helpers.R"))
source(file.path(proj_root, "helpers", "paper_figures.R"))
derived <- file.path(proj_root, "data", "derived")

boot_bundle <- readRDS(file.path(derived, "bootstrap_2019.rds"))
exp_bundle  <- readRDS(file.path(derived, "expectation_2019.rds"))
```

## 1. Synthetic-coder performance

```{r}
#| label: fig-landscape
#| fig-cap: "Synthetic coder performance: greedy (mode) vs expectation (mean) readout."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.2
fig_readout_landscape(exp_bundle, boot_bundle, band = "human_loo")
```

# Appendix

## A1. B and F hypothesis tests

```{r}
#| label: fig-bf
#| fig-cap: "Paired ΔMAE for the registered B and F contrasts, with the zero line and ±SESOI band."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.8
fig_bf(boot_bundle)
```

## A2. Full model × input grid

```{r}
#| label: fig-grid
#| fig-cap: "Every model on every input (the off-diagonal expansion of Figure 1). Greedy (mode) vs expectation (mean) MAE with country-clustered 95% CIs. Rings mark each fine-tuned model's own training input (the diagonal). Dashed line = naive persistence model; long-dash line = human reference; grey band = ±SESOI around the human reference."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 9
fig_readout_grid(exp_bundle, boot_bundle, band = "human_loo")
```
